definition_en: to have a different opinion, or to fail to match or suit something
core_image: 两个人隔着桌子，一个摇头，一个把杯子往前一推
scene: 会议桌上摊着两份预算，谁也没有去碰对方那张纸。She disagreed with every point in the report.
sceneCN: 这里 disagreed 指「不同意」（第 1 个义项：意见不同）；句意是报告里的每一点她都不同意。

senses.title: To hold a different opinion
senses.definition: to think that another person's view is wrong
senses.definitionCN: 认为别人的看法不对
senses.example: She disagreed with every point in the report.
senses.exampleCN: 报告里的每一点她都不同意。
senses.why: Two people can look at one page and see two different worlds.
senses.whyCN: 两个人看同一页纸，却看见两个不同的世界。

senses.title: To fail to match
senses.definition: to be different from something that should be the same
senses.definitionCN: 与本应相同的东西对不上
senses.example: The two accounts disagree on the time of the call.
senses.exampleCN: 两份记录对通话时间的说法不一致。
senses.why: When two records part company, at least one of them is wrong.
senses.whyCN: 两份记录一旦分道，至少有一份是错的。

senses.title: To upset the body
senses.definition: to make a person feel unwell, said of food or weather
senses.definitionCN: 指食物或气候让人身体不舒服
senses.example: Rich food disagrees with my stomach.
senses.exampleCN: 油腻的食物让我的胃不舒服。
senses.why: The body argues with what it cannot accept.
senses.whyCN: 身体接受不了的东西，它会自己争辩。

intro.en: Disagree is the negative prefix dis- added to agree, a verb English took from Old French agreer.
intro.cn: disagree 是否定前缀 dis- 加 agree，而 agree 来自古法语 agreer。

items.en: Gratus meant pleasing or welcome.
items.cn: gratus 指令人愉快的、受欢迎的。

items.en: Agreer meant to please or to be to someone's liking.
items.cn: agreer 指使人高兴，或合某人的意。

items.en: Agree first meant to please, then to be of one mind.
items.cn: agree 先指使人满意，后指意见一致。

items.en: Disagree reversed that harmony into a clash of views.
items.cn: disagree 把这份和谐翻转成观点的冲撞。

items.en: The verb also covers records that do not match and food that upsets.
items.cn: 这个词也用于对不上的记录与让身体不适的食物。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the agree stem, while the meaning group names different ways of standing against someone.
note.cn: 形近组共用 agree 这一段词干，近义组则区分几种与人相左的方式。

entries.definition: to have the same opinion as someone
a state in which people hold different views
unpleasant or hard to get along with
entries.definitionCN: 令人不快或难以相处的

entries.definition: to be unlike, or to hold another view
entries.definitionCN: 不相同，或持另一种看法

entries.definition: to argue that something is not true
to say that one is against something

normalIntro.en: These hooks move from two heads shaking at a table to a stomach turning against rich food.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从桌边两个摇头的人，走到受不了油腻食物的胃。

normal.en: Dis- plus agree is agreement pulled apart.
normal.cn: dis- 加 agree，就是把一致拆开。

normal.en: Agree to disagree ends the argument without ending the friendship.
normal.cn: agree to disagree 结束了争论，却没结束交情。

normal.en: Two clocks that disagree cannot both be right.
normal.cn: 两只走时不一致的钟，不可能都对。

normal.en: When food disagrees with you, the stomach writes a protest.
normal.cn: 食物跟你不对付时，胃会写一封抗议信。

normal.en: To disagree is not to hate; it is only to see otherwise.
normal.cn: 不同意不等于厌恶，只是看到了别的样子。

abstract.en: Picture two hands pulling one sheet of paper in opposite directions.
abstract.cn: 想象两只手朝相反方向拉同一张纸。

abstract.en: Picture two clocks showing different hours on one wall.
abstract.cn: 想象同一面墙上两只钟指着不同的时间。

abstract.en: Picture a plate pushed away half finished.
abstract.cn: 想象一盘吃了一半就被推开的菜。

examples.en: I disagree with your first reason.
examples.cn: 我不同意你的第一个理由。

examples.en: The two reports disagree about the number of deaths.
examples.cn: 两份报告对死亡人数的说法不一致。

examples.en: They disagreed for an hour and then went home.
examples.cn: 他们争了一个小时，然后各自回家。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 disagree 记成「的士格瑞」：两个人为了打车费的哥争执起来，谁也不让谁。

root: 由否定前缀 dis- 加 agree 构成。agree 来自古法语 agreer，源头是拉丁语 gratus（令人愉快的），本指合意、使人满意，后来才表示意见一致；加 dis- 之后，就表示看法不合、对不上，甚至让身体不适。

sensesIntro.en: From two minds that will not meet, to two records that will not match, to a body that refuses its food.
sensesIntro.cn: 从谈不拢的两个心思，到对不上的两份记录，再到拒绝食物的身体。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two hands pulling the same sheet of paper apart.
core.cn: 核心意象：两只手把同一张纸往两边拉。

chain: TWO PEOPLE READ THE SAME PAGE

branches.en: The first sense is two minds that will not meet.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是两个谈不拢的心思。

branches.en: The second sense is two records that will not match.
branches.cn: 第二个义项是两份对不上的记录。

branches.en: The third sense is a body that refuses what it is given.
branches.cn: 第三个义项是拒绝所受之物的身体。

branches.en: People and papers both show the gap by failing to line up.
branches.cn: 人和纸都靠对不齐来显出那道缝。

branches.en: A clash of views and a clash in the stomach both end in discomfort.
branches.cn: 看法相撞与胃里相撞，最后都不舒服。

intro.en: Disagree gathers the agree family, words about harmony, consent and its opposite.
intro.cn: disagree 聚起 agree 一族词，围绕和睦、同意与相反面。

latinIntro.en: Latin gratus, pleasing, passed through Old French agreer and gave the base agree.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 gratus（令人愉快）经古法语 agreer 传下，给出词基 agree。

items.example: They disagree about the cause of the fire.
items.exampleCN: 他们对起火原因意见不一。

items.example: We agree on the main point.
items.exampleCN: 我们在要点上看法一致。

items.meaning: a state of shared opinion or a formal deal
items.example: The two sides signed an agreement.
A small disagreement grew into a quarrel.
items.exampleCN: 一点小分歧变成了争吵。

items.example: He can be a disagreeable guest.
items.exampleCN: 他有时是个让人不舒服的客人。

items.example: She gave an agreeable answer.
items.exampleCN: 她给了一个让人舒服的回答。

items.example: They met at the agreed place.
items.exampleCN: 他们在商定的地点见了面。

items.example: The room smelled disagreeably of smoke.
items.exampleCN: 屋里有一股难闻的烟味。

definition_en: to stop being seen, or to stop existing
core_image: 魔术师把布一掀，桌上的鸟笼空了，只剩一根羽毛
scene: 灯忽然灭了，台上的人影没了，观众还以为这是节目的一部分。The coin seemed to disappear between his fingers.
sceneCN: 这里 disappear 指「消失」（第 1 个义项：看不见了）；句意是那枚硬币在他指间好像消失了。

senses.title: Out of sight
senses.definition: to pass out of sight so that the eye can no longer find it
senses.definitionCN: 离开视线，眼睛再也找不到
senses.example: The coin seemed to disappear between his fingers.
senses.exampleCN: 那枚硬币在他指间好像消失了。
senses.why: What the eye cannot follow, the mind cannot keep.
senses.whyCN: 眼睛跟不上的东西，脑子也留不住。

senses.title: Missing without explanation
senses.definition: to be lost or to go missing, often leaving no trace
senses.definitionCN: 走失或不见，往往不留痕迹
senses.example: Two hikers disappeared in the fog.
senses.exampleCN: 两名徒步者在雾里失踪了。
senses.why: The empty place asks a question that has no answer yet.
senses.whyCN: 那块空出来的地方，问出一个还没有答案的问题。

senses.title: Gone for good
senses.definition: to stop existing, as a species or a custom does
senses.definitionCN: 像物种或习俗那样不再存在
senses.example: Many old crafts are disappearing from the village.
senses.exampleCN: 村里许多老手艺正在消失。
senses.why: The last one goes, and nothing in the world can be asked again.
senses.whyCN: 最后一个没了，世上就再没有谁可以问了。

intro.en: Disappear is dis- added to appear, which comes from Latin apparere, to come into sight.
intro.cn: disappear 是 dis- 加 appear，而 appear 来自拉丁语 apparere（出现在眼前）。

items.en: Apparere meant to come into view or become visible.
items.cn: apparere 指进入视野或变得可见。

items.en: The prefix ad- added the sense of coming toward a place.
items.cn: 前缀 ad- 添上「朝某处而来」的意思。

items.en: Appear entered English meaning to come in sight.
items.cn: appear 进入英语，意为出现在眼前。

items.en: Disappear reversed it into going out of sight.
items.cn: disappear 把它反过来，表示离开视线。

items.en: The word widened to missing people and vanishing species.
items.cn: 这个词后来扩展到失踪的人与消失的物种。

note.en: The look-alike group plays with appear and its forms, while the meaning group names ways of leaving no trace.
note.cn: 形近组围绕 appear 及其形式，近义组则列出几种不留痕迹的离开。

entries.definition: to come into sight
the act of coming into sight, or the way something looks
entries.definitionCN: 出现这一动作，或某物的外表

entries.definition: easy to see or understand, or seeming true
entries.definitionCN: 显而易见的，或表面看来如此的

entries.definition: to disappear suddenly and completely
to grow weaker until it cannot be seen
to turn into vapour and vanish from sight
entries.definitionCN: 化为蒸气而从眼前消失

normalIntro.en: These hooks move from a coin hidden in a palm to a craft that leaves a village for good.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从藏在掌心的硬币，走到永远离开村庄的手艺。

normal.en: Dis- means away, so disappear is to take away the appearance.
normal.cn: dis- 是「离开」，disappear 就是把出现带走。

normal.en: The coin disappears because the hand closes.
normal.cn: 硬币之所以不见，是因为手掌合上了。

normal.en: A person disappears when no one can say where.
normal.cn: 一个人失踪，是没人说得出他在哪儿。

normal.en: A custom disappears when the last hand stops doing it.
normal.cn: 一门习俗消失，是最后一双手不再做了。

normal.en: What disappears leaves an outline where it used to be.
normal.cn: 消失的东西，会在原来的位置留下一个轮廓。

abstract.en: Picture a palm opening over an empty table.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手掌在空桌上摊开。

abstract.en: Picture fog closing over a path.
abstract.cn: 想象雾把小径合拢起来。

abstract.en: Picture a birdcage with the door open and no bird.
abstract.cn: 想象一只鸟笼门开着，里面没有鸟。

examples.en: The sun disappeared behind the hills.
examples.cn: 太阳落到山后不见了。

examples.en: Her bag disappeared from the table.
examples.cn: 她的包从桌上不见了。

examples.en: Whole species are disappearing as the forest shrinks.
examples.cn: 随着森林缩小，整个物种正在消失。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 disappear 记成「的士皮儿」：的士一开走，扬起的皮儿都散了，人影也没了。

root: 由否定前缀 dis- 加 appear 构成。appear 来自拉丁语 apparere（出现在眼前），词根 parere 意为露面。加前缀后表示离开视线，后来又从「看不见」扩展到「失踪」与「彻底不存在」。

sensesIntro.en: From a coin lost between fingers, to a person lost in fog, to a whole species lost for good.
sensesIntro.cn: 从指间不见的硬币，到雾里失踪的人，再到永远消失的整个物种。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an open palm over an empty table.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只摊开的手掌下面，桌子空了。

chain: THE HAND CLOSES OVER A COIN

branches.en: The first sense is simply being out of sight.
branches.cn: 第一个义项就是单纯地离开视线。

branches.en: The second sense is a person no one can locate.
branches.cn: 第二个义项是没人找得到的人。

branches.en: The third sense is a kind of thing gone from the world.
branches.cn: 第三个义项是从世上消失的一类东西。

branches.en: A hidden coin and a missing walker both leave a searching eye.
branches.cn: 藏起的硬币和失踪的行人，都留下一双寻找的眼睛。

branches.en: One is lost for a while; the other is lost for good.
branches.cn: 一个只是暂时丢了，另一个是永远没了。

intro.en: Disappear belongs to the appear family, words about coming into view and leaving it.
intro.cn: disappear 属于 appear 一族，围绕出现与离开视线。

latinIntro.en: Latin apparere, to come into sight, is the source of appear and of disappear.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 apparere（出现在眼前）是 appear 与 disappear 的源头。

items.example: The ship disappeared into the mist.
A light appeared at the end of the road.
items.exampleCN: 路尽头出现了一点灯光。

items.meaning: the act of appearing or the look of a thing
items.example: His sudden appearance surprised us.
items.exampleCN: 他的突然出现让我们吃了一惊。

items.meaning: easy to see or seeming to be true
items.example: It was apparent that she had been crying.

items.meaning: as far as one can see or judge
items.example: Apparently the shop closed last month.
items.exampleCN: 那家店看来上个月就关了。

items.meaning: the act of vanishing or being lost
items.example: The police studied his sudden disappearance.
items.exampleCN: 警方调查他的突然失踪。

items.example: The moon reappeared after the clouds passed.
items.exampleCN: 云过去后月亮又出来了。

items.meaning: in the act of going out of sight
items.example: He watched the disappearing shore.
items.exampleCN: 他望着渐渐消失的海岸。

definition_zh: 使失望；使希望落空；使受挫
definition_en: to fail to satisfy someone's hope or expectation
core_image: 拆开的礼物盒里躺着一张写错的卡片，孩子的笑停在半路
scene: 他拆开信封，看了两行就把它折回去。The ending disappointed everyone who had waited a year.
sceneCN: 这里 disappointed 指「使失望」（第 1 个义项：没能满足期待）；句意是那个结局让等了一年的人都失望了。

derivatives.zh: 失望；令人失望的人或事

senses.title: To let someone down
senses.definition: to make a person feel sad because what was hoped for did not happen
senses.definitionCN: 因所盼望的没有实现而让人难过
senses.example: The ending disappointed everyone who had waited a year.
senses.exampleCN: 那个结局让等了一年的人都失望了。
senses.why: The picture in the mind was brighter than the thing in the hand.
senses.whyCN: 脑子里的画面，比手里拿到的东西更亮。

senses.title: To fall short of a hope
senses.definition: to fail to reach the standard that was expected
senses.definitionCN: 没有达到所期待的水平
senses.example: The film disappointed the hopes of its young fans.
senses.exampleCN: 这部电影让年轻影迷的希望落了空。
senses.why: A promise is measured only after it has been kept or broken.
senses.whyCN: 承诺只有在守住或落空之后，才量得出长短。

senses.title: To defeat a plan
senses.definition: to prevent a plan or purpose from being carried out
senses.definitionCN: 使计划或目的无法实现
senses.example: Heavy rain disappointed our plan for the day.
senses.exampleCN: 大雨打乱了当天的计划。
senses.why: A plan can be broken by weather as easily as by a person.
senses.whyCN: 计划能被一个人打破，也能被一场雨打破。

intro.en: Disappoint came from Old French desappointer, to remove from a post, built on point, a fixed place.
intro.cn: disappoint 来自古法语 desappointer（免职），词基 point 指固定的位置。

items.en: Punctum meant a point or a small hole, the base of point.
items.cn: punctum 指点或小孔，是 point 的词源。

items.en: Apointier meant to arrange or to set a matter in place.
items.cn: apointier 指安排妥当，把事情放到位置上。

items.en: Desappointer meant to remove someone from an appointment.
items.cn: desappointer 指解除某人的职位。

items.en: English used disappoint for removing a person from office.
items.cn: 英语最初用 disappoint 表示免除某人的职务。

items.en: The sense shifted from losing a post to losing a hope.
items.cn: 词义从失去职位，转向失去一份期待。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the appoint stem, while the meaning group names other ways of failing a hope.
note.cn: 形近组共用 appoint 这一段词干，近义组则列出其他让希望落空的方式。

entries.definition: to choose someone for a job or position
a fixed time to meet, or a job given to someone
entries.definitionCN: 约定的会面时间，或授予的职位

entries.definition: sad because a hope was not met
entries.definitionCN: 因希望未实现而难过的

entries.definition: to fail to help or support someone who trusted you
to prevent a hope or plan from succeeding
entries.definitionCN: 使希望或计划无法实现

entries.definition: to make someone feel shock and loss of hope
entries.definitionCN: 使某人震惊并失去希望

normalIntro.en: These hooks move from a gift that misses its mark to a plan broken by rain.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从没送到心上的礼物，走到被雨打乱的计划。

normal.en: Dis- plus appoint: the appointment is taken away.
normal.cn: dis- 加 appoint：本来说好的位置被拿走了。

normal.en: A gift that misses the wish disappoints the hand.
normal.cn: 送不到心愿上的礼物，会让接的手失望。

normal.en: Disappointed is the face; disappointing is the cause.
normal.cn: disappointed 是那张脸，disappointing 是那个原因。

normal.en: A film can disappoint a whole row of fans at once.
normal.cn: 一部电影能同时让一整排影迷失望。

normal.en: The word once meant losing a post, now it means losing a hope.
normal.cn: 这个词从前指丢了职位，如今指丢了希望。

abstract.en: Picture a gift box open with the wrong card inside.
abstract.cn: 想象礼盒打开，里面放错了卡片。

abstract.en: Picture a smile that stops halfway.
abstract.cn: 想象一个笑到一半停住的表情。

abstract.en: Picture a paper plan soaked by rain.
abstract.cn: 想象一张被雨泡软的计划纸。

examples.en: I did not mean to disappoint you.
examples.cn: 我不是有意让你失望。

examples.en: The result disappointed everyone in the team.
examples.cn: 结果让队里每个人都失望了。

examples.en: His second book disappointed the critics.
examples.cn: 他的第二本书让评论界失望了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 disappoint 记成「的士破印」：约好的的士没来，车票上的印也破了，等的人自然失望。

root: 来自古法语 desappointer，本义是解除某人的职位，词基 point 指点、位置，出自拉丁语 punctum。进入英语后先表示免职，后来词义转向「使期待落空」，因为失去职位正是最直接的失望。

sensesIntro.en: From a person whose hope is not met, to a standard that is not reached, to a plan that cannot go on.
sensesIntro.cn: 从希望没被满足的人，到没达到的标准，再到无法继续的计划。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a gift box open, and the card inside says the wrong name.
core.cn: 核心意象：礼盒打开，里面的卡片写着错的名字。

branches.en: The first sense is the person whose hope is let down.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是希望被辜负的那个人。

branches.en: The second sense is the standard that is not reached.
branches.cn: 第二个义项是没能达到的那条标准。

branches.en: The third sense is the plan that cannot move forward.
branches.cn: 第三个义项是走不下去的计划。

branches.en: A person and a promise are judged by the same gap.
branches.cn: 人和承诺，都是用同一道落差来衡量的。

branches.en: A hope and a plan both end where reality refuses them.
branches.cn: 希望和计划，都停在现实不答应的地方。

intro.en: Disappoint gathers the appoint family, words about posts, promises and let-downs.
intro.cn: disappoint 聚起 appoint 一族词，围绕职位、约定与辜负。

latinIntro.en: Point and appoint go back to Latin punctum, a point or a fixed place.
latinIntro.cn: point 与 appoint 都可追到拉丁语 punctum（点、固定位置）。

items.meaning: to fail to meet a hope
items.example: The news disappointed the whole family.

items.meaning: to choose someone for a post
items.example: They appointed her as head of the team.
items.exampleCN: 他们任命她为团队负责人。

items.meaning: a fixed meeting or a post given to someone
items.example: I have an appointment at four.
She looked disappointed by the answer.
It was a disappointing season.
items.exampleCN: 那是个令人失望的赛季。

items.meaning: the feeling of being let down
items.example: He hid his disappointment well.

items.meaning: in a way that lets people down
items.example: The machine worked disappointingly slowly.
items.exampleCN: 这台机器慢得让人失望。

items.meaning: to choose someone for a post again
items.example: The board reappointed him for two years.

definition_en: an event that causes great damage or suffering, or a complete failure
core_image: 风暴过后，屋顶掀开一半，一把椅子挂在树枝上
scene: 水退到脚踝，墙上留着一条深色的线，家具全倒了。The flood was the worst disaster in the town's history.
sceneCN: 这里 disaster 指「灾难」（第 1 个义项：造成巨大损失的事件）；句意是这场洪水是该镇历史上最严重的灾难。

senses.title: An event of great harm
senses.definition: a sudden event such as a flood or fire that causes great damage
senses.definitionCN: 洪水、火灾之类突然造成巨大损失的事件
senses.example: The flood was the worst disaster in the town's history.
senses.exampleCN: 这场洪水是该镇历史上最严重的灾难。
senses.why: The world keeps its shape, but people lose theirs.
senses.whyCN: 世界还保持着形状，人的日子却散了。

senses.title: A complete failure
senses.definition: a plan or event that fails completely
senses.definitionCN: 彻底失败的计划或活动
senses.example: The concert was a disaster from the first note.
senses.exampleCN: 那场音乐会从第一个音起就是一场灾难。
senses.why: Nobody is hurt, and yet everything has fallen down.
senses.whyCN: 没有人受伤，可所有东西都塌了。

senses.title: A hopeless person
senses.definition: a person who is completely unable to do something well
senses.definitionCN: 完全做不好某件事的人
senses.example: He is a disaster in the kitchen.
senses.exampleCN: 他在厨房里简直一塌糊涂。
senses.why: The word lends its ruin to one clumsy pair of hands.
senses.whyCN: 这个词把自己的废墟，借给了一双笨手。

intro.en: Disaster came from Italian disastro, literally an ill star, and carried the old belief that stars shaped events.
intro.cn: disaster 来自意大利语 disastro，字面是「凶星」，带着星辰左右世事的旧观念。

items.en: Astrum meant a star, and astronomy read the sky for signs.
items.cn: astrum 指星辰，占星与天象之学都从天上找征兆。

items.en: Disastro joined dis-, bad, to astro, star.
items.cn: disastro 把表示「坏」的 dis- 与 astro（星）合在一起。

items.en: Desastre carried the word into French with the same sense.
items.cn: desastre 以同样的意思把词带进法语。

items.en: English disaster named a calamity blamed on an unlucky star.
items.cn: 英语 disaster 指归咎于凶星的灾祸。

items.en: The star faded, and the word kept only the ruin.
items.cn: 星辰的意味淡去，这个词只留下了废墟。

note.en: The look-alike group differs by a letter or two, while the meaning group names other large misfortunes.
note.cn: 形近组只差一两个字母，近义组则列出其他巨大的不幸。

entries.definition: a large dry area of land with little rain
sweet food eaten at the end of a meal
causing great harm or failure
entries.definitionCN: 造成巨大损害或失败的

entries.definition: an event that causes great and sudden suffering
entries.definitionCN: 造成巨大而突然苦难的事件

entries.definition: a serious misfortune that brings deep distress
entries.definitionCN: 带来深切痛苦的严重不幸

entries.definition: a very sad event, especially one involving death
entries.definitionCN: 极悲惨的事件，尤指涉及死亡的

normalIntro.en: These hooks move from a storm over a town to a kitchen ruined by one cook.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从笼罩小镇的风暴，走到被一个厨子弄乱的厨房。

normal.en: Dis- plus aster: a bad star was once blamed for every ruin.
normal.cn: dis- 加 aster：从前每场废墟都怪一颗凶星。

normal.en: A natural disaster arrives without asking.
normal.cn: 自然灾害从不先打招呼。

normal.en: A party can be a disaster and still be remembered fondly.
normal.cn: 一场聚会可能是灾难，却仍被人笑着记住。

normal.en: Disaster relief arrives after the water, not before.
normal.cn: 救灾总是在水来之后，而不是之前。

normal.en: One clumsy cook can turn a kitchen into a disaster area.
normal.cn: 一个笨厨子就能把厨房变成灾区。

abstract.en: Picture a roof half lifted off a house.
abstract.cn: 想象屋顶被掀开了一半。

abstract.en: Picture a chair hanging from a tree branch.
abstract.cn: 想象一把椅子挂在树枝上。

abstract.en: Picture a dark line left high on a wall by water.
abstract.cn: 想象墙上高处留着一条水退后的深色线。

examples.en: The earthquake was a disaster for the whole region.
examples.cn: 这场地震对整个地区是一场灾难。

examples.en: Poor planning turned the event into a disaster.
examples.cn: 糟糕的筹划把这场活动变成了灾难。

examples.en: Several disasters struck the coast that year.
examples.cn: 那一年海岸遭遇了好几次灾害。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 disaster 记成「地砸死他」：地一塌，砸下来，就是一场灾难。

root: 来自意大利语 disastro，字面意思是「凶星」，由表示坏的 dis- 与 astro（星辰）组成。古人相信星辰决定祸福，于是把大祸归因于星象。这个词经法语进入英语后，星辰的意味逐渐淡去，只留下灾难与彻底失败的意思。

sensesIntro.en: From a flood that ruins a town, to an evening that ruins itself, to a cook who ruins dinner.
sensesIntro.cn: 从毁掉小镇的洪水，到自我毁掉的夜晚，再到毁掉晚饭的厨子。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a house with its roof half gone and a chair in the tree.
core.cn: 核心意象：屋顶没了一半，椅子挂在树上。

branches.en: The first sense is the great event that harms many.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是伤害许多人的巨大事件。

branches.en: The second sense is a failure with no injury.
branches.cn: 第二个义项是没有伤人却彻底失败的事。

branches.en: The third sense lends that ruin to one hopeless person.
branches.cn: 第三个义项把这片废墟借给一个没救的人。

branches.en: A flood and a concert can both end in the same wreckage.
branches.cn: 洪水和音乐会，都可能收在同样的残局里。

branches.en: A failed evening and a failing cook share one word.
branches.cn: 失败的夜晚和失败的厨子，共用一个词。

intro.en: Disaster opens the star family: disaster, disastrous, and the astro- words.
intro.cn: disaster 打开了「星辰」一族：disaster、disastrous 以及 astro 系列。

latinIntro.en: Latin astrum, star, and Greek astron, star, give the astro- base in this family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 astrum 与希腊语 astron 都指星辰，给出这一族的 astro 词基。

items.example: The fire was a disaster for the village.
items.exampleCN: 那场火对村子是一场灾难。

items.example: The decision had a disastrous effect.
items.exampleCN: 那个决定造成了灾难性的后果。

items.meaning: in a way that causes ruin
items.example: The plan failed disastrously.

items.meaning: a small rocky body in space
items.example: An asteroid passed close to the earth.
items.exampleCN: 一颗小行星从地球附近掠过。

items.meaning: the study of stars and their supposed influence
items.example: She reads astrology for fun.

items.meaning: the scientific study of stars and space
items.example: He teaches astronomy at the university.
The astronomer mapped the southern sky.
items.exampleCN: 那位天文学家绘制了南天星图。

items.meaning: a star-shaped mark used in printing
items.example: A small asterisk marks the note.
items.exampleCN: 一个小星号标出了注释。

definition_en: a flat round object, a disc that stores sound or data, or a pad between bones
core_image: 一片薄薄的圆盘在灯下转，边缘反出一圈白光
scene: 唱机的手臂落下，圆盘开始转，屋里响起沙沙的底噪。He slid the disc into the player.
sceneCN: 这里 disc 指「光盘」（第 1 个义项：扁圆形的存储介质）；句意是他把光盘推进了播放机。

derivatives.zh: 迪斯科舞曲；迪斯科舞厅

senses.title: A round carrier of sound or data
senses.definition: a thin round object on which music or computer data is stored
senses.definitionCN: 存着音乐或电脑数据的薄圆片
senses.example: He slid the disc into the player.
senses.exampleCN: 他把光盘推进了播放机。
senses.why: A whole evening of sound hides in one shiny circle.
senses.whyCN: 一整个晚上的声音，藏在一个发亮的圆里。

senses.title: Any flat round object
senses.definition: a flat circular thing, such as a plate of metal
senses.definitionCN: 扁平的圆形物体，如一片金属盘
senses.example: The machine cuts a disc from the steel sheet.
senses.exampleCN: 机器从钢板上切下一个圆盘。
senses.why: The shape is older than any use people found for it.
senses.whyCN: 这个形状比人给它找的任何用途都更老。

senses.title: A pad between bones
senses.definition: a soft round pad that sits between the bones of the spine
senses.definitionCN: 夹在脊椎骨之间的软圆垫
senses.example: A damaged disc can press on a nerve.
senses.exampleCN: 受损的椎间盘会压到神经。
senses.why: Even the body keeps small round cushions between hard parts.
senses.whyCN: 连身体也要在硬骨之间垫上小圆垫。

intro.en: Disc goes back through Latin discus to Greek diskos, a flat round plate thrown in games.
intro.cn: disc 经拉丁语 discus 追溯到希腊语 diskos，指比赛中掷出的扁圆盘。

items.en: Diskos named a quoit, a flat stone or metal plate thrown in sport.
items.cn: diskos 指比赛里掷出的扁石盘或金属盘。

items.en: Discus borrowed the Greek word for the same object.
items.cn: discus 借来这个希腊词，指同样的东西。

items.en: Disc and disk entered English for a flat round surface.
items.cn: disc 与 disk 进入英语，指扁平的圆面。

items.en: Records and then compact discs gave the word a musical life.
items.cn: 唱片与后来的激光唱片，让这个词有了音乐的生命。

items.en: It now also names a cushion between spinal bones.
items.cn: 如今它也指脊椎骨之间的软垫。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the disc- shape, while the meaning group names other round flat things.
note.cn: 形近组共用 disc 这一形状词干，近义组则列出其他扁圆之物。

entries.definition: a flat round object or a computer storage device
a style of dance music with a strong beat
entries.definitionCN: 节奏强烈的迪斯科舞曲

entries.definition: a heavy disc thrown in an athletics event
entries.definitionCN: 田径比赛中掷出的重圆盘

entries.definition: a flat round dish used for food
a round plastic disc that carries recorded sound
entries.definitionCN: 录有声音的圆形塑料唱片

entries.definition: a large flat plate, or an old record disc

normalIntro.en: These hooks move from a spinning plate of sound to a soft pad inside the spine.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从旋转的发声圆盘，走到脊椎里的软垫。

normal.en: Disc is a shape before it is a thing.
normal.cn: disc 先是一个形状，然后才是一件东西。

normal.en: A disc jockey turns two round plates into a night.
normal.cn: 唱片骑师把两张圆盘转成一个夜晚。

normal.en: Scratch a disc and the music stumbles.
normal.cn: 光盘一划伤，音乐就会打结。

normal.en: A slipped disc is a small cushion out of place.
normal.cn: 椎间盘突出，就是一个小软垫挪了位。

normal.en: The same round shape serves music, machines and the body.
normal.cn: 同一个圆形，服务音乐、机器与身体。

abstract.en: Picture a thin silver circle catching the light.
abstract.cn: 想象一个薄薄的银圆接住灯光。

abstract.en: Picture a needle settling into a groove.
abstract.cn: 想象唱针落进一道细槽。

abstract.en: Picture two bones with a soft round pad between them.
abstract.cn: 想象两块骨头之间垫着一个软圆垫。

examples.en: He slid the disc into the player.
examples.cn: 他把光盘推进了播放机。

examples.en: The disc was scratched and skipped.
examples.cn: 光盘划伤了，播放时跳音。

examples.en: The doctor found a damaged disc in her back.
examples.cn: 医生发现她背部有一处椎间盘受损。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 disc 记成「碟斯克」：碟子一样的圆片，就是 disc。

root: 来自希腊语 diskos（掷出的扁圆盘），经拉丁语 discus 进入英语，最初指扁平的圆面。后来唱片、激光光盘先后借用这个词，使它有了承载声音与数据的意思；医学上又用它指脊椎骨之间的软垫。

sensesIntro.en: From a shiny circle that holds music, to any flat round plate, to a cushion inside the spine.
sensesIntro.cn: 从装着音乐的亮圆片，到任何扁圆盘，再到脊椎里的软垫。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a thin round plate spinning under a light.
core.cn: 核心意象：一片薄圆盘在灯下旋转。

chain: DATA IS BURNED IN TINY DOTS
A SOFT PAD SITS BETWEEN BONES

branches.en: The first sense is the round carrier of sound or data.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是承载声音或数据的圆片。

branches.en: The second sense is the bare shape itself.
branches.cn: 第二个义项是那个形状本身。

branches.en: The third sense is the body's own small disc.
branches.cn: 第三个义项是身体里自带的小圆盘。

branches.en: Music and metal both borrow the same flat circle.
branches.cn: 音乐与金属借用了同一个扁圆。

branches.en: A pad between bones is a disc no one can see.
branches.cn: 骨间的软垫，是一只看不见的圆盘。

intro.en: Disc gathers a family of round and flat words, from disks to discus.
intro.cn: disc 聚起一族与圆、扁有关的词，从磁盘到铁饼。

latinIntro.en: Greek diskos and Latin discus, a thrown plate, give the base disc-.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊语 diskos 与拉丁语 discus（掷出的圆盘）给出词基 disc。

items.example: The disc lay face down on the desk.
items.exampleCN: 那张光盘正面朝下放在桌上。

items.meaning: a flat round object or storage device
items.example: The file is saved on the disk.
The party played disco all night.
items.exampleCN: 聚会整晚都在放迪斯科。

items.meaning: a heavy disc thrown in sport
items.example: He threw the discus across the field.

items.meaning: a person who plays recorded music
items.example: The disc jockey kept the crowd dancing.
items.exampleCN: 唱片骑师让全场一直跳着。

items.meaning: a machine part that reads discs
items.example: The disc drive would not open.

items.meaning: brakes that press on a round plate
items.example: The bike has disc brakes on both wheels.
items.exampleCN: 这辆车的两个轮子都装了盘式刹车。

items.meaning: having the form of a flat circle
items.example: The nest was disc-shaped and shallow.

definition_en: training that produces obedience and control, a field of study, or punishment
core_image: 操场上鞋跟并拢的响声，一排人影在晨光里排成直线
scene: 天还没亮，哨声一响，所有人从床上弹起，几十秒后站成四列。Good discipline kept the team calm under pressure.
sceneCN: 这里 discipline 指「纪律」（第 1 个义项：让人守规矩的约束）；句意是良好的纪律让团队在压力下保持冷静。

senses.title: Training that makes people obey
senses.definition: training and rules that produce order and self-control
senses.definitionCN: 带来秩序与自制的训练和规则
senses.example: Good discipline kept the team calm under pressure.
senses.exampleCN: 良好的纪律让团队在压力下保持冷静。
senses.why: A line of people moves as one only when each one holds still.
senses.whyCN: 一排人只有各自站住，才能像一个整体那样动。

senses.title: A field of study
senses.definition: a branch of knowledge studied in school or research
senses.definitionCN: 在学校或研究中钻研的一个知识分支
senses.example: She studies two disciplines at once.
senses.exampleCN: 她同时学两门学科。
senses.why: A mind in training is organised like a body in training.
senses.whyCN: 受训的心，和受训的身体一样有条理。

senses.title: To punish and correct
senses.definition: to train someone by punishment or firm control
senses.definitionCN: 用惩罚或严格管束来训练某人
senses.example: The teacher disciplined the class firmly.
senses.exampleCN: 老师严格管教了这个班。
senses.why: The word turns from the rule into the hand that enforces it.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从规矩本身，转成执行规矩的那只手。

intro.en: Discipline comes from Latin disciplina, instruction, from discere, to learn, and discipulus, a learner.
intro.cn: discipline 来自拉丁语 disciplina（教导），词根 discere 意为学习，discipulus 指学习者。

items.en: Discere meant to learn, and discipulus meant a learner.
items.cn: discere 指学习，discipulus 指学习者。

items.en: Disciplina named teaching, knowledge and orderly conduct.
items.cn: disciplina 指教导、知识以及有秩序的行为。

items.en: Discipline carried the sense of instruction and correction.
items.cn: 这个词在古法语里兼指教导与纠正。

items.en: English discipline meant training, especially of the mind.
items.cn: 英语里的 discipline 指训练，尤指心智的训练。

items.en: It widened to a field of study and to punishment.
items.cn: 它后来扩展到学科，也指惩罚。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the discip- stem, while the meaning group names order, training and correction.
note.cn: 形近组共用 discip 这一段词干，近义组则区分秩序、训练与纠正。

entries.definition: a person who follows and learns from a teacher
connected with the punishment of faults
able to control one's own behaviour
the process of teaching a skill through practice
entries.definitionCN: 通过练习教授技能的过程

entries.definition: a state in which everything is in its right place
a penalty given for a wrong act
entries.definitionCN: 对错误行为施加的惩处

normalIntro.en: These hooks move from a whistle at dawn to a subject that trains the mind.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从黎明的一声哨响，走到一门训练心智的学问。

normal.en: Discipline and disciple share a root: both are about learning.
normal.cn: discipline 与 disciple 同根，都和学习有关。

normal.en: A line of shoes on a field is discipline you can see.
normal.cn: 操场上排齐的鞋，是看得见的纪律。

normal.en: Self-discipline is a whistle nobody has to blow.
normal.cn: 自律是一声不需要别人吹的哨。

normal.en: A discipline is also a subject, trained like a muscle.
normal.cn: 学科也是一门功夫，要像肌肉一样练。

normal.en: To discipline a child is to teach, not only to punish.
normal.cn: 管教孩子是为了教，不只是为了罚。

abstract.en: Picture four rows of shadows standing perfectly still.
abstract.cn: 想象四排影子一动不动地站着。

abstract.en: Picture a whistle cutting through cold morning air.
abstract.cn: 想象一声哨响划过清冷的晨空。

abstract.en: Picture a notebook filled with the same careful hand.
abstract.cn: 想象一本笔记，全是同样工整的字迹。

examples.en: Good discipline kept the team calm under pressure.
examples.cn: 良好的纪律让团队在压力下保持冷静。

examples.en: She studies two disciplines at once.
examples.cn: 她同时学两门学科。

examples.en: The teacher disciplined the class firmly.
examples.cn: 老师严格管教了这个班。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 discipline 记成「地是三坡林」：地在三面坡上，林子里的人也得排好队，讲的就是纪律。

root: 来自拉丁语 disciplina（教导），词根是 discere（学习），同源词 discipulus 指学习者。它先指对心智与行为的训练，后来既指一群人遵守的秩序，也指学校里的一门学问，还引申为用惩罚来纠正。

sensesIntro.en: From a body trained to stand in line, to a mind trained in one field, to the hand that corrects.
sensesIntro.cn: 从被训练得站成一条线的身体，到在一个领域受训的心，再到那只纠正人的手。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: rows of people standing still at the sound of a whistle.
core.cn: 核心意象：哨声一响，一排排人静静站定。

branches.en: The first sense is the order that training produces.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是训练带来的秩序。

branches.en: The second sense is the field a trained mind works in.
branches.cn: 第二个义项是受训的心所钻研的领域。

branches.en: The third sense is the correction that keeps the order.
branches.cn: 第三个义项是维持秩序的纠正。

branches.en: A trained body and a trained mind follow the same habit.
branches.cn: 受训的身体和心智，遵循同一种习惯。

branches.en: Without correction, the line slowly bends.
branches.cn: 没有纠正，那条线就会慢慢弯掉。

intro.en: Discipline gathers the discip- family, words about learning, order and correction.
intro.cn: discipline 聚起 discip 一族词，围绕学习、秩序与纠正。

latinIntro.en: Latin discere, to learn, gives discipulus, a learner, and disciplina, teaching.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 discere（学习）给出 discipulus（学习者）与 disciplina（教导）。

items.example: The school is known for its discipline.
items.exampleCN: 这所学校以纪律严明著称。

items.meaning: a learner who follows a teacher
items.example: He was a disciple of the old master.
items.exampleCN: 他是那位老大师的弟子。

items.example: She is a disciplined worker.
The company began a disciplinary hearing.

items.meaning: a person who enforces strict rules
items.example: The coach was a firm disciplinarian.
items.exampleCN: 这位教练纪律要求很严。

items.meaning: the act of training or correcting
items.example: Disciplining a child takes patience.

senses.exampleCN: 这家店给学生打九折。

senses.title: To treat something as unlikely

intro.en: Discount came from dis- plus count, literally to count off a part, and passed through Italian and French.
intro.cn: discount 是 dis- 加 count，字面是「扣掉一部分再算」，经意大利语与法语传来。

items.en: Computare meant to reckon together, the base of count.
items.cn: computare 指合起来计算，是 count 的词源。

items.en: Disconto named a sum counted off from a debt.
items.cn: disconto 指从欠款里扣掉的数目。

items.en: Descompte carried the money sense into French trade.
items.cn: descompte 把这个钱的用法带进法国商业。

items.en: Discount named money taken off a price.
items.cn: discount 指从价钱里减去的钱。

items.en: The verb widened to mean treating an idea as not worth counting.

sensesIntro.en: From money taken off a price, to the act of lowering it, to a risk left out of the count.

latinIntro.en: Latin computare, to reckon together, gives count, account and discount.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 computare（合起来计算）给出 count、account 与 discount。

definition_en: to find something or learn a fact for the first time
core_image: 草丛被拨开，地上露出一只从没被记录的脚印
scene: 雨后的泥地很软，他蹲下去看那串新鲜的痕迹。She discovered a hidden path behind the house.
sceneCN: 这里 discover 指「发现」（第 1 个义项：找到原本存在却不为人知的东西）；句意是她发现屋后有一条隐蔽的小路。

collocations.phrase: discover that the door was open

senses.title: To come upon what was hidden
senses.definition: to find something that existed before but was not known
senses.definitionCN: 找到原本存在却不为人知的东西
senses.example: Scientists discovered a new kind of frog.
senses.exampleCN: 科学家发现了一种新的青蛙。
senses.why: A page turns, and a room that was always there appears.
senses.whyCN: 翻过一页，一间一直都在的屋子忽然出现。

senses.title: To learn a fact
senses.definition: to learn or realize something you did not know before
senses.definitionCN: 得知或意识到自己原先不知道的事
senses.example: I discovered that the shop closes at six.
senses.exampleCN: 我发觉那家店六点关门。
senses.why: The world does not change; only your picture of it does.
senses.whyCN: 世界没变，变的是你心里那张图。

intro.en: Discover is Latin dis-, undoing, plus cooperire, to cover: to take the cover off something.
intro.cn: discover 是拉丁语 dis-（去掉）加 cooperire（覆盖），本义是把盖子揭开。

items.en: Cooperire meant to cover something completely.
items.cn: cooperire 指把东西完全盖住。

items.en: Dis- undid that cover, so the thing stood bare.
items.cn: 前缀 dis- 把覆盖去掉，东西就露了出来。

items.en: Descovrir meant to uncover or lay bare.
items.cn: 古法语 descovrir 指揭开覆盖、露出本来面目。

items.en: English took it as to reveal or find out.
items.cn: 英语借入时表示揭露或查明。

items.en: The word now covers a lucky find and a slow research.
items.cn: 今天它既指偶然碰上，也指长期研究所得。

note.en: The look-alike group keeps the cover stem, and the meaning group lists other ways of finding.
note.cn: 形近组保留 cover 这段词干，近义组列出别的表示找到的词。

to remove a cover or bring to light
the act or result of finding

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with a lifted cover and end with a fact that fits into place.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从揭开的盖子开始，落到终于对上位置的一件事。

normal.en: Dis- plus cover: take the cover off.
normal.cn: dis 加 cover，就是把盖子揭开。

normal.en: A child discovers a beetle under a stone.
normal.cn: 孩子在石头下面发现一只甲虫。

normal.en: You discover the truth when two stories stop matching.
normal.cn: 两个说法对不上时，你就发现了真相。

normal.en: A discovered path shortens the walk home.
normal.cn: 发现的小路让回家的路变短。

normal.en: Science discovers slowly, one careful step at a time.
normal.cn: 科学发现很慢，一次只走一小步。

abstract.cn: 想象一块布从桌面被拉开。

abstract.cn: 想象手电的光在黑暗里找到一扇门。

abstract.cn: 想象地图上一段空白被填上名字。

examples.en: We discovered that the train had already left.
examples.cn: 我们发觉火车已经开走了。

examples.en: The team discovered a new cave last summer.
examples.cn: 去年夏天那支队伍发现了一个新洞穴。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 discover 记成「揭开盖子」：dis 是去掉，cover 是盖子，盖子一揭，藏着的东西就露出来。

root: 源自拉丁语 cooperire（覆盖）加否定前缀 dis-，经古法语 descovrir 进入英语，本义是揭开覆盖之物。后来从「露出」引申为「找到原本就在那里、只是没人知道的东西」，也指得知一件事实。

sensesIntro.en: From lifting a cover off something hidden to learning a plain fact about the world.
sensesIntro.cn: 从揭开藏物上的覆盖，到得知世上的一件普通事实。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a cloth lifted, and something that was always there stands revealed.
core.cn: 核心意象：布被掀开，一直都在的东西露了出来。

branches.en: The first sense is the moment a hidden thing shows itself.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是藏物露出来的那一刻。

branches.en: The second sense moves the find inside the mind, as knowledge.
branches.cn: 第二个义项把发现搬进心里，变成知识。

branches.en: Both senses begin with something unknown and end with it known.
branches.cn: 两个义项都从不知道开始，到知道为止。

branches.en: Both can happen by accident or by long search.
branches.cn: 两个义项都可能是偶然，也可能是长久的寻找。

branches.en: Only the second sense can be a small everyday fact.
branches.cn: 只有第二个义项可以是一件日常小事。

intro.en: Discover sits in the cover family, where dis-, un- and re- each change what the cover does.
intro.cn: discover 属于 cover 一族，前缀 dis-、un-、re- 改变的都是盖子被怎样处理。

latinIntro.en: Latin cooperire, to cover, gives the stem cover-, which carries dis-, un- and re- in turn.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 cooperire（覆盖）给出词干 cover，依次接上 dis-、un- 与 re-。

senses.title: The act of finding

senses.whyCN: 同一堵墙走过多年，终于有一天停了下来。

senses.title: The thing that is found

senses.example: The old coin turned out to be an important discovery.
senses.exampleCN: 那枚旧硬币后来成了重要发现。
senses.why: A find is small enough to hold, yet it redraws the whole field.
senses.whyCN: 一件发现小得可以捧在手里，却把整片领域重画。

intro.en: Discovery is discover plus -y; the stem goes back to Latin dis- and cooperire, to uncover.
intro.cn: discovery 是 discover 加名词后缀 -y；词干可追到拉丁语 dis- 与 cooperire（揭开覆盖）。

items.en: Cooperire meant to cover, and dis- meant the opposite.
items.cn: cooperire 指覆盖，dis- 表示相反的动作。

items.en: Descovrir, to uncover, entered French from that Latin pair.
items.cn: descovrir 由这对拉丁成分进入法语，意为揭开。

items.en: The verb discover came first, meaning to reveal.
items.cn: 先有动词 discover，表示揭露。

items.en: The noun discovery named the act and later the thing found.
items.cn: 名词 discovery 先指行为，后也指找到的东西。

items.en: Science gave it the weight of a formal result.
items.cn: 科学语境让它带上了正式成果的分量。

note.en: The look-alike group is built on the discover stem, and the meaning group names other kinds of finds.

examples.cn: 那条隧道的发现改变了整个计划。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 discovery 记成「揭开盖子看见的东西」：dis 去掉，cover 盖子，-y 变名词，揭盖之后所见就是发现。

root: 由动词 discover 加名词后缀 -y 构成；discover 源自拉丁语 cooperire（覆盖）加 dis-，经古法语 descovrir 进入英语，本义是揭开覆盖。因此 discovery 既指揭开的过程，也指被揭出来的东西。

sensesIntro.en: From the act of lifting a cover to the object that lies underneath.
sensesIntro.cn: 从揭开覆盖的动作，到覆盖底下那件东西。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a red circle closing around a name that was not on the map before.
core.cn: 核心意象：红笔圈住一个从前不在图上的名字。

branches.en: The first sense is the work and the moment of finding.

intro.en: Discovery sits at the noun end of the cover family: discover, discoverer, discoverable.
intro.cn: discovery 站在 cover 一族的名词一端，同族还有 discover、discoverer 与 discoverable。

latinIntro.en: Latin cooperire, to cover, yields cover and discover, and the suffix -y makes the finding a thing.

items.meaning: the act or result of finding

items.example: The pattern is discoverable in the data.
items.exampleCN: 这个规律在数据里可以被发现。

items.meaning: a finding again of something old

definition_en: to talk about something with others, or to examine a subject in speech or writing
core_image: 几个人围着一张桌子，手指在纸上来回点
scene: 桌上摊着一张计划表，几根手指同时点向同一行。We need to discuss the budget before Friday.

senses.title: To exchange views on a subject
senses.definition: to talk about a subject with other people and hear different views

senses.title: To examine a subject in writing
senses.definition: to examine a subject in speech or writing in an organized way

senses.exampleCN: 报告论述了失败的三个原因。
senses.why: A page can hold a conversation that nobody is having aloud.
senses.whyCN: 一页纸能装下一场没人出声的对话。

intro.en: Discuss comes from Latin discutere, to strike apart, built from dis- and quatere, to shake.
intro.cn: discuss 来自拉丁语 discutere（打散、击碎），由 dis- 与 quatere（摇、击）组成。

items.en: Quatere meant to shake or strike.
items.cn: quatere 指摇动或击打。

items.en: Discutere meant to strike apart and so to examine closely.
items.cn: discutere 指打散，因而引申为细查。

items.en: English took it as to examine or argue a case.
items.cn: 英语借入时表示审查或争辩一个案子。

items.en: The sense settled into talking a matter over.
items.cn: 词义固定为把事情谈开。

items.en: Writing can discuss a subject without any voice at all.
items.cn: 书面文字也能论述主题，不必有声音。

note.en: The look-alike group comes from the discuss stem, and the meaning group gathers other forms of talk.
note.cn: 形近组来自 discuss 词干，近义组聚起别的谈话形式。

entries.definition: a conversation about a subject
a person who takes part in a discussion
talked about by many people
a formal argument with two sides
to give reasons for or against something
entries.definitionCN: 为赞成或反对给出理由

entries.definition: to talk something over with others

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with fingers on one line and end with a page that keeps the talk.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从手指点在同一行开始，落到一页留住谈话的纸。

normal.en: Dis- plus cuss: the matter is struck apart for a look.
normal.cn: dis 加 cuss，就是把事情打散来看。

normal.en: Two engineers discuss a crack until the cause is clear.
normal.cn: 两个工程师讨论一道裂纹，直到原因清楚。

normal.en: Families discuss money best at a table, not at a door.
normal.cn: 一家人谈钱，最好在桌边，不在门口。

normal.en: The report discusses what the meeting only hinted at.
normal.cn: 报告论述了会上只隐约提到的部分。

normal.en: A discussed problem is half solved.
normal.cn: 被讨论过的问题，已经解决了一半。

abstract.en: Picture four fingers tapping the same line.
abstract.cn: 想象四根手指点在同一行上。

abstract.en: Picture a sheet turned round and round.
abstract.cn: 想象一张纸被转来转去。

abstract.en: Picture a pen drawing a line under one word.
abstract.cn: 想象笔在一个词底下画了一道。

examples.en: We need to discuss the budget before Friday.
examples.cn: 我们得在周五前讨论预算。

examples.en: The article discusses three reasons for the change.
examples.cn: 这篇文章论述了这一变化的三个原因。

examples.en: They discussed the matter for two hours.
examples.cn: 他们商量这件事商量了两个小时。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 discuss 记成「把话打散」：dis 是分开，cuss 与击打同源；把一件事敲碎摊开，大家一块看，就是讨论。

root: 源自拉丁语 discutere（打散、细查），由 dis-（分开）与 quatere（摇、击）构成，本义是把东西击碎摊开来看。进入英语后先指审查辩论，后来固定为「讨论」，再引申出书面上的「论述」。

sensesIntro.en: From striking a matter apart to see its pieces, to the calm page that sets them in order.
sensesIntro.cn: 从把一件事打散看清各块，到把各块摆整齐的那页文字。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: several fingers tapping the same line on one sheet of paper.
core.cn: 核心意象：几根手指同时点在同一张纸的同一行上。

branches.en: The first sense is the round of voices at the table.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是桌边一轮又一轮的声音。

branches.en: The second sense lets the page do the talking later.
branches.cn: 第二个义项让纸页在事后替人说话。

branches.en: Both take a subject apart before putting it together.
branches.cn: 两个义项都先拆开话题，再把它拼上。

branches.en: Both can be long, slow and unfinished.
branches.cn: 两个义项都可能漫长、缓慢、没有结论。

branches.en: Only the second sense appears in print.
branches.cn: 只有第二个义项会出现在印刷品里。

intro.en: Discuss keeps the Latin stem cuss-, to strike, which also hides inside percussion.
intro.cn: discuss 保留拉丁词干 cuss-（击打），这个词干也藏在 percussion 里。

latinIntro.en: Latin quatere, to shake, becomes -cuss- in discuss and discussus in the past participle.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 quatere（摇动）在 discuss 中变成 cuss-，过去分词是 discussus。

items.example: They discussed the map at length.
items.exampleCN: 他们详细讨论了那张地图。

items.meaning: a conversation that examines a subject
items.example: The discussion lasted an hour.

items.meaning: one who takes part in a discussion
items.example: Each discussant had five minutes.
The terms are still discussable.
One point remained undiscussed.
The plan was widely discussed.

items.meaning: in the act of talking over
items.example: They sat discussing the letter.

items.meaning: a striking through, as on a drum
items.example: Percussion opened the piece.
items.exampleCN: 打击乐为这首曲子开场。

definition_en: a conversation in which people share views on a subject, or a written treatment of it
core_image: 一张写满字的纸被推到桌子中间，几个人轮流指着其中一行
scene: 纸页被推到桌子中间，几个人轮流指着上面的一行。The discussion lasted until the lights went out.
sceneCN: 这里 discussion 指「讨论」（第 1 个义项：交换看法的谈话）；句意是讨论一直持续到熄灯。

senses.title: A conversation of shared views
senses.definition: a conversation in which people exchange views on a subject
senses.definitionCN: 人们就某个话题交换看法的谈话
senses.example: The discussion lasted until midnight.
senses.exampleCN: 讨论一直持续到半夜。
senses.why: A table of voices is cheaper than a table of mistakes.
senses.whyCN: 一桌人的声音，比一桌错误便宜。

senses.title: A written treatment of a subject
senses.definition: a section of writing that examines a subject in detail
senses.definitionCN: 详细探讨某一主题的书面部分
senses.example: The final chapter is a discussion of risk.
senses.exampleCN: 最后一章是对风险的论述。
senses.why: The talk leaves the room and becomes a page.
senses.whyCN: 谈话离开屋子，变成一页纸。

intro.en: Discussion is discuss plus -ion, from Latin discutere, to strike apart and examine.
intro.cn: discussion 是 discuss 加 -ion，源自拉丁语 discutere（打散、细查）。

items.en: Discutere meant to shake a thing apart.
items.cn: discutere 指把东西摇散。

items.en: The participle discussus described a thing broken open.
items.cn: 过去分词 discussus 形容被打开的东西。

items.en: The noun first named a formal examination of a case.
items.cn: 这个名词最早指对案子的正式审查。

items.en: It came to mean a talk among several people.
items.cn: 后来指几个人之间的谈话。

items.en: Essays now carry discussion as a named section.
items.cn: 如今文章里也用 discussion 作章节名。

note.en: The look-alike group keeps the discuss stem, and the meaning group lists other kinds of exchange.
note.cn: 形近组保留 discuss 词干，近义组列出别的交流方式。

entries.definition: to talk a subject over
a person who joins a discussion
talked about by other people
a formal exchange of opposing views
an informal talk between people
a talk that aims at understanding
entries.definitionCN: 以求理解为目的的对话

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with a sheet pushed to the middle and end with a chapter that keeps it.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从推到桌中的一张纸开始，落到把它留下的一章。

normal.en: Discussion is discuss plus -ion, the talk turned into a noun.
normal.cn: discussion 是 discuss 加 -ion，把谈话变成名词。

normal.en: A group discussion needs one quiet listener to work.
normal.cn: 小组讨论需要一个安静的听众才成。

normal.en: Under discussion means the answer is still moving.
normal.cn: 在讨论中，意思是答案还在动。

normal.en: A panel discussion puts five voices in one row.
normal.cn: 专家讨论把五个声音排成一排。

normal.en: The discussion section of a paper admits what is still unknown.
normal.cn: 论文的论述部分会承认还未知的事。

abstract.en: Picture a sheet sliding to the centre of a table.
abstract.cn: 想象一张纸滑到桌子中央。

abstract.en: Picture a hand raised to take the next turn.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手举起，准备接下一轮。

abstract.en: Picture a lamp still on after everyone has agreed.
abstract.cn: 想象大家说定之后，灯还亮着。

examples.en: The discussion lasted until the lights went out.
examples.cn: 讨论一直持续到熄灯。

examples.en: We had a long discussion about the new rules.
examples.cn: 我们就新规定进行了长时间的讨论。

examples.en: Her paper ends with a discussion of memory.
examples.cn: 她的论文以一节关于记忆的论述收尾。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 discussion 记成「打散之后的谈」：discuss 是把事敲开来看，加 -ion 就成了这一场谈，也指纸上那一节论述。

root: 由动词 discuss 加名词后缀 -ion 构成；源头是拉丁语 discutere（打散、细查）。英语里先指对案件的正式审查，后指多人之间的谈话，现代又用作论文中「讨论」这一章节的名称。

sensesIntro.en: From a room full of voices to a chapter that keeps the voices in order.
sensesIntro.cn: 从一屋子声音，到把这些声音排整齐的一章。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a written sheet pushed to the middle of a table.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张写满字的纸被推到桌子中间。

branches.en: The first sense is the living talk around the table.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是桌边活生生的谈话。

branches.en: The second sense is the same talk pressed into print.
branches.cn: 第二个义项是同一场谈话压进纸里。

branches.en: Both senses hold several views in one place.
branches.cn: 两个义项都把几种看法收在一处。

branches.en: Both can end without a decision.
branches.cn: 两个义项都可能没有结论就结束。

branches.en: Only the second sense has a page number.
branches.cn: 只有第二个义项带页码。

intro.en: Discussion is the noun built on discuss, inside the small cuss- family from Latin quatere.
intro.cn: discussion 是由 discuss 构成的名词，属于拉丁语 quatere 衍生的 cuss- 小家族。

latinIntro.en: Latin discutere, to shake apart, gives discuss and discussion, with -ion marking the act.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 discutere（摇散）给出 discuss 与 discussion，后缀 -ion 标出行为。

items.meaning: the act of talking a subject over
items.example: The discussion was calm.
They discuss the plan weekly.
items.exampleCN: 他们每周讨论这个计划。

items.example: A discussant asked about cost.
items.exampleCN: 一位讨论者问到了成本。

items.example: The price remains discussable.
The risk went undiscussed.
The topic was much discussed.
items.exampleCN: 这个话题被讨论了很多。

items.example: They were discussing the map.
items.exampleCN: 他们正在讨论那张地图。

items.meaning: a striking, as on a drum
items.example: The percussion was too loud.

definition_en: an illness of the body or mind, or a serious problem in a society
core_image: 一片叶子上出现一块褐色斑点，几天后整枝都软了
scene: 叶面上先出现一个褐色小点，几天后整片叶子都软了。The disease spread through the whole orchard in a month.
sceneCN: 这里 disease 指「疾病」（第 1 个义项：身体或精神的病症）；句意是那种病一个月内传遍了整片果园。

senses.title: An illness of the body
senses.definition: an illness that affects the body or mind
senses.definitionCN: 影响身体或精神的病症
senses.example: The disease spread through the orchard.
senses.exampleCN: 那种病传遍了果园。
senses.why: A small spot on one leaf is a whole orchard a month later.
senses.whyCN: 一片叶子上的小点，一个月后就是整片果园。

senses.title: A sickness in society
senses.definition: a serious problem that harms a group or a system
senses.definitionCN: 危害群体或制度的严重问题
senses.example: Greed is a disease of the market.
senses.exampleCN: 贪婪是市场的一种弊病。
senses.why: The same word moves from one body to a body of people.
senses.whyCN: 同一个词从一具身体挪到一群人身上。

intro.en: Disease comes from Old French desaise, a lack of ease, built from des- and aise, comfort.
intro.cn: disease 来自古法语 desaise（不适、不安），由 des-（不）与 aise（安适）构成。

items.en: Adiacens meant lying near, and gave the French word for comfort.
items.cn: adiacens 意为躺卧在旁，后来给出法语里表示安适的词。

items.en: Desaise meant lack of ease or discomfort.
items.cn: 古法语 desaise 指不安适、不舒服。

items.en: English disease first meant unease of any kind.
items.cn: 英语 disease 最初泛指任何不适。

items.en: It narrowed to a named illness of the body.
items.cn: 后来收窄为身体上具体的病症。

items.en: The old sense survives in the idea of a social disease.
items.cn: 旧义在社会弊病这一说法里还留有余影。

note.en: The look-alike group is built on ease, and the meaning group names other words for being unwell.
note.cn: 形近组围绕 ease 构成，近义组列出别的表示身体不适的词。

entries.definition: comfort or freedom from effort
not calm or comfortable
suffering from an illness
the state of being unwell
a feeling of being ill
a small or lasting disorder

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with one brown spot and end with a word for a broken system.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从一个褐色斑点开始，落到一个形容坏制度的词。

normal.en: Dis- plus ease: no ease is disease.
normal.cn: dis 加 ease，失去安适就是病。

normal.en: A garden left alone shows disease first on the oldest leaf.
normal.cn: 无人打理的花园，最老的叶子先显出病。

normal.en: Doctors name a disease so that they can fight one thing.
normal.cn: 医生给病取名，才好集中对付一样东西。

normal.en: A disease of the market hides in plain prices.
normal.cn: 市场的弊病藏在平常的价钱里。

normal.en: Clean water is the cheapest guard against disease.
normal.cn: 干净的水是对抗疾病最便宜的守卫。

abstract.en: Picture one brown spot spreading across a leaf.
abstract.cn: 想象一个褐色斑点爬满一片叶子。

abstract.en: Picture a lamp held over a sick branch at night.
abstract.cn: 想象夜里一盏灯照着病枝。

abstract.en: Picture a word moving from a body to a whole town.
abstract.cn: 想象一个词从一具身体挪到整座城。

examples.en: The disease spread through the whole orchard in a month.
examples.cn: 那种病一个月内传遍了整片果园。

examples.en: Clean water prevents many diseases.
examples.cn: 干净的水能预防许多疾病。

examples.en: Greed is a disease of the market.
examples.cn: 贪婪是市场的一种弊病。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 disease 记成「不自在」：dis 是不，ease 是安适，身体不安适就是病；一个群体不安适，就是弊病。

root: 来自古法语 desaise（不适），由否定前缀 des- 与 aise（安适）构成，而 aise 可追到拉丁语 adiacens（躺卧在旁）。英语最初泛指各种不适，十六世纪起收窄为具体的病症，后来又引申指社会的弊病。

sensesIntro.en: From a body that has lost its ease to a system that has lost its health.
sensesIntro.cn: 从一具失去安适的身体，到一个失去健康的制度。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one brown spot on a leaf, and the whole orchard going soft.
core.cn: 核心意象：叶上一个褐色斑点，整片果园慢慢软下去。

branches.en: The first sense is the illness in a living body.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是活身体里的病症。

branches.en: The second sense carries the illness into a system.
branches.cn: 第二个义项把病带进一个制度。

branches.en: Both senses describe something that spreads by itself.
branches.cn: 两个义项都形容会自己蔓延的东西。

branches.en: Both need a name before they can be fought.
branches.cn: 两个义项都要先有名字才好对付。

branches.en: Only the second sense is used about money or power.
branches.cn: 只有第二个义项会用在金钱或权力上。

intro.en: Disease belongs to the ease family, where comfort, difficulty and illness share one stem.
intro.cn: disease 属于 ease 一族，安适、容易与疾病共用同一词干。

latinIntro.en: Old French aise, comfort, joins des- to make desaise, and English keeps several relatives of the same stem.
latinIntro.cn: 古法语 aise（安适）加 des- 成为 desaise，英语保留了同一词干的几个亲属。

items.example: The disease moved fast.
She swam with ease.
The first step was easy.
The glass broke easily.
He felt uneasy at the door.
A small unease stayed with her.
The diseased tree was cut down.
The plants are disease-free.

definition_en: a strong feeling of dislike, or to make someone feel this
core_image: 一个人闻到坏掉的食物，脸往后一缩
scene: 他低头闻了闻那碗放了三天的汤，立刻把脸转开。The smell of the bin filled her with disgust.
sceneCN: 这里 disgust 指「厌恶」（第 1 个义项：强烈的反感）；句意是垃圾桶的气味让她满心厌恶。

senses.title: A strong feeling of dislike
senses.definition: a strong feeling of dislike caused by something unpleasant
senses.definitionCN: 由不快之物引起的强烈反感
senses.example: She turned away in disgust.
senses.exampleCN: 她厌恶地转过身。
senses.why: The body pulls back before the mind finds a word.
senses.whyCN: 身体先退开，脑子才找到词。

senses.title: To cause that feeling
senses.definition: to make someone feel strong dislike
senses.definitionCN: 让人产生强烈反感
senses.example: The mess disgusted everyone in the room.
senses.exampleCN: 那堆脏乱让屋里每个人都反感。
senses.why: A smell can push a whole room toward the door.
senses.whyCN: 一种气味能把整屋子人推向门口。

intro.en: Disgust comes from Old French desgouster, to lose the taste for something, from des- and goust, taste.
intro.cn: disgust 来自古法语 desgouster（失去胃口），由 des- 与 goust（味道）构成。

items.en: Gustus meant taste, and gustare meant to taste.
items.cn: gustus 指味道，gustare 指品尝。

items.en: Desgouster meant to lose the taste for something.
items.cn: 古法语 desgouster 指对某物失去胃口。

items.en: English disgust meant a strong distaste.
items.cn: 英语 disgust 指强烈的反胃感。

items.en: The verb added the sense of causing that distaste.
items.cn: 动词又添上使人产生这种反感的意思。

items.en: It now covers moral repulsion as well as bad food.
items.cn: 今天它既指食物难吃，也指道德上的反感。

note.en: The look-alike group is built on Latin gustus, taste, and the meaning group names stronger forms of dislike.
note.cn: 形近组建在拉丁语 gustus（味道）上，近义组列出更强的反感。

entries.definition: a sudden rush of wind
lively enjoyment in doing something
causing strong dislike
a very strong feeling of disgust
a mild dislike of something
to drive someone away by being unpleasant
entries.definitionCN: 因令人不快而使人退开

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with a bowl gone bad and end with a whole room stepping back.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从一碗变质的汤开始，落到整屋子人一起后退。

normal.en: Dis- plus gust: the taste turns against you.
normal.cn: dis 加 gust，味道反过来对付你。

normal.en: Milk left out for a day can disgust a child.
normal.cn: 牛奶在外放一天，能让孩子反胃。

normal.en: A dirty kitchen disgusts more than a loud argument.
normal.cn: 脏厨房比大声争吵更让人反感。

normal.en: Disgusted, he pushed the plate away unseen.
normal.cn: 他一阵反感，悄悄把盘子推开。

normal.en: Some lies disgust people who tell small ones daily.
normal.cn: 有些谎话会让天天说小谎的人也反感。

abstract.en: Picture a spoon lifted and then set down fast.
abstract.cn: 想象勺子举起又飞快放下。

abstract.en: Picture a face turned toward the window.
abstract.cn: 想象一张脸转向窗户。

abstract.en: Picture a hand held over the nose and mouth.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手捂住口鼻。

examples.en: The smell of the bin filled her with disgust.
examples.cn: 垃圾桶的气味让她满心厌恶。

examples.en: He looked at the dirty plate in disgust.
examples.cn: 他厌恶地看着那只脏盘子。

examples.en: The state of the kitchen disgusted the inspector.
examples.cn: 厨房的状况让检查员十分反感。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 disgust 记成「坏了胃口」：dis 表示相反，gust 是味道，尝到坏味道就反胃，进而厌恶。

root: 来自古法语 desgouster（失去胃口），由 des-（相反）与 goust（味道）构成，goust 可追到拉丁语 gustus。本义是食物让人反胃，后来从口舌的感觉扩展到对行为与人品的强烈反感。

sensesIntro.en: From a mouth that refuses food to a mind that refuses a deed.
sensesIntro.cn: 从一张拒绝食物的嘴，到一颗拒绝某种行为的心。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a face pulled back from a bowl that has gone bad.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张脸从变质的碗边往后缩。

branches.en: The first sense is the feeling inside the body.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是身体里升起的那种感觉。

branches.en: The second sense is the thing that puts it there.
branches.cn: 第二个义项是把它放进身体的那件事。

branches.en: Both senses turn on a loss of appetite.
branches.cn: 两个义项都围绕胃口的失去。

branches.en: Both begin in the nose before they reach the mind.
branches.cn: 两个义项都先到鼻子，再到心里。

branches.en: Only the second sense needs an object in front of you.
branches.cn: 只有第二个义项需要眼前有个对象。

intro.en: Disgust belongs to the Latin gustus family, where taste and wind share one small stem.

items.en: Discus meant a flat round object thrown in games.

sensesIntro.cn: 从一只扁圆的盘子，到一座城因之得名的那道菜。

intro.en: Dish belongs to the disc family, where a flat round shape turns into a plate and then into a recipe.

latinIntro.en: Latin discus, a flat round object, passes through disc into dish, and the same stem also gives disk.

senses.title: A flat round object

intro.en: Disk and disc both come from Latin discus, a flat round object thrown in games and set on tables.
intro.cn: disk 与 disc 同出拉丁语 discus，既指游戏中投掷的扁圆物，也指桌上的平盘。

items.en: Diskos meant a quoit thrown in competition.
items.cn: diskos 指比赛中投掷的铁饼。

items.en: Discus kept both the game piece and the table plate.
items.cn: discus 同时保留游戏器具与餐桌平盘两义。

items.en: English used disc for a round flat thing.
items.cn: 英语用 disc 指圆而扁的东西。

items.en: American spelling disk named the computer medium.
items.cn: 美式拼写 disk 用来指计算机存储介质。

items.en: Disc stays for sound and light, disk for data.

note.en: The look-alike group shares the flat round shape, and the meaning group names other round holders.

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with a bright circle and end with a room full of memory.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从一个亮圆片开始，落到一间装满记忆的屋子。

normal.en: Disk is a flat round thing, like a coin with no face.
normal.cn: disk 是扁圆之物，像一枚没有图案的硬币。

normal.en: A hard disk hides behind a metal box.
normal.cn: 硬盘藏在一只金属盒子后面。

normal.en: Disk space runs out exactly when you need it.

normal.en: The same shape holds music, film and files.

abstract.en: Picture a silver circle spinning under a lamp.
abstract.cn: 想象一个银圆片在灯下旋转。

examples.cn: 文件存在硬盘上。

examples.en: He handed me a disk with the photos.
examples.cn: 他递给我一张存着照片的磁盘。

examples.en: A disk of polished steel covered the hole.
examples.cn: 一块抛光钢圆盘盖住了那个洞。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 disk 记成「扁圆片」：disk 与 dish 同源，都是拉丁语 discus 那种扁圆的东西，电脑把数据也放进了这样的圆片。

root: 源自拉丁语 discus（投掷用的扁圆物），其根可追到希腊语 diskos。英语里 disc 与 disk 原本只是拼写差异，二十世纪以后逐渐分工：disc 多指唱片与光盘，disk 多指计算机的磁盘与硬盘。

sensesIntro.en: From a quoit thrown in a game to a quiet surface that keeps our files.
sensesIntro.cn: 从比赛中投出的铁饼，到安静保存文件的那个面。

latinIntro.en: Greek diskos and Latin discus give disc and disk, two spellings of one flat round idea.

definition_en: to remove someone from a job, or to refuse to consider an idea
core_image: 一扇门被推开，里面的人抱着纸箱走出来

sceneCN: 这里 dismiss 指「解雇」（第 1 个义项：让人失去工作）；句意是经理毫无预警地解雇了两名工人。

collocations.zh: 把某人当成空想家而不予理会

senses.title: To send someone from a job

senses.example: The manager dismissed two workers.
senses.exampleCN: 经理解雇了两名工人。
senses.why: A desk is cleared in minutes, a name in seconds.

senses.title: To refuse to consider

senses.title: To let people leave

senses.why: A wave of the hand can empty a room politely.
senses.whyCN: 一挥手，就能礼貌地清空一间屋子。

intro.en: Dismiss comes from Latin dimittere, to send away, made of dis-, apart, and mittere, to send.
intro.cn: dismiss 来自拉丁语 dimittere（遣散），由 dis-（分开）与 mittere（送）构成。

items.en: Mittere meant to send or to let go.
items.cn: mittere 指送出或放开。

items.en: Dimittere meant to send people away in different directions.
items.cn: dimittere 指把人往各处遣散。

items.en: Desmettre meant to put away or release.
items.cn: 古法语 desmettre 指放走、解除。

items.en: English dismiss meant to send away a crowd.
items.cn: 英语 dismiss 指遣散一群人。

items.en: The sense of removing from a post became common.
items.cn: 免职这一义在十九世纪通行。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the dismiss stem, and the meaning group names other ways of pushing someone out.

normal.en: A case dismissed is not a case forgotten.
